issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) specifies Animal.messageOnFeed() as returning a String, and the song/printing logic in the template expects string messages. However, the solution implementation changes the signature to return a FeedResponse object (Animal.messageOnFeed(): FeedResponse, and Pig/Seal return new FeedResponse(...)). This signature mismatch is structural and will confuse students about the expected return type and how to implement/print feed messages.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the return type of messageOnFeed across all artifacts. Either: (A) Change the solution to match the specification by making Animal.messageOnFeed() return String and update Pig/Seal/Goat to return the feed message String (and remove or adapt FeedResponse), or (B) Update the problem statement, template, and tests to document/expect a FeedResponse return type (and adjust song/printing logic to use FeedResponse.getMessage()). Prefer option A to match the current problem description and UML.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Animal.messageOnFeed() as returning a String, but the solution introduces a new FeedResponse type and declares Animal.messageOnFeed() to return FeedResponse. This changes the expected method return type (and adds a new conceptual entity FeedResponse) which students will not find or expect from the problem description or the template. The mismatch creates a mapping/confusion when implementing and printing feed messages (problem/template expect direct String messages, solution returns an object).
issues.suggestedFix: Choose one consistent contract for messageOnFeed(): either (A) follow the problem statement and UML and have messageOnFeed() return String everywhere (remove FeedResponse and update solution implementations to return String), or (B) update the problem statement and template to document the new FeedResponse return type and explain the FeedResponse semantics. Align template, tests, and solution to the same return type so students can map the requirement unambiguously.
